canonical.title: Longest Bitonic Subsequence
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/7. DP on LIS/04. Longest Bitonic Subsequence.cpp

narrative.title: The Cable-Car Ridge Profile
narrative.scenario: A mountain railway records the elevations of n pylons. A scenic route must climb strictly over a stretch of pylons and then descend strictly over the rest — a mountain shape. The survey team wants the longest such ride measured in pylons visited; a pure climb or a pure descent also counts as scenic.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n positive integers (pylon elevations).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the length of the longest subsequence that is strictly increasing then strictly decreasing (either flank may be empty).

testCases.explanation: A pure climb qualifies with an empty descent flank.

hintLevels: Level 1: Every bitonic chain has one summit — measure the climb into it and the fall out of it separately.
Level 2: Compute LIS ending at i and LDS starting at i; combine as left[i] + right[i] - 1.
Level 3: The -1 removes the double-counted summit; scan all summits and take the max.
